spec_features.spec_quote: an agent loop that attempts each task for a bounded number of turns
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:78 `for turn in range(max_turns):` bounds the attempt loop; max_turns flows config.py:20 (default 8) -> runner.py:53 -> agent.run_episode(max_turns=...). The loop terminates when range is exhausted, ending the episode.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced end-to-end: the for-range loop caps attempts and stops the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 8 # attempts per task before we give up  ...  # Budgets (held CONSTANT across regression runs so the stimulus is fixed)

spec_features.feature_name: loop stops on success or budget exhaustion
spec_features.spec_quote: model produces an attempt... loop continues until success (never, for rigged) or budget exhausted
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:92-95 `if verdict.passed: ep.solved = True; break` provides the success exit; the range(max_turns) at agent.py:78 provides budget-exhaustion exit. Both branches actually execute. For rigged tasks RiggedExecutor.run always returns passed=False (executor.py), so only the budget exit fires.
spec_features.notes: Both stop conditions are wired and run; success simply never occurs for rigged tasks by construction, so the operative bound is the turn budget.

spec_features.spec_quote: I am deliberately not making triggers-per-dollar the headline optimization target
spec_features.evidence: metrics.py:48 reports `trigger_rate` as primary and cost as secondary (cost_per_trigger_usd:metrics.py); analysis.compare() bases verdict on trigger_rate delta + two-proportion z (analysis.py:55,60-65), with cost only reported. So trigger_rate-at-fixed-budget is what the code actually computes/compares.
spec_features.notes: There is no optimizer to constrain, so 'not optimizing triggers-per-dollar' is not an active guard; what IS implemented is that trigger_rate is the metric compared and cost is informational only. Partial: real metric wiring, but the 'don't optimize cost' claim itself has no enforcing mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Primary: trigger_rate with a 95% Wilson confidence interval. ... Secondary, reported metric ... cost is for budgeting regression runs, not the optimization target.

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness must not put catastrophizing words in the model's mouth
spec_features.evidence: rig_feedback.py:23 assert_neutral() scans text against AFFECT_BLOCKLIST (rig_feedback.py:15-19) and raises ValueError on a match; it is called on every feedback string at rig_feedback.py:86 inside feedback_for(), which is the function RiggedExecutor.run() (executor.py) uses to produce feedback shown to the subject. So goading text actually aborts the run.
spec_features.notes: Enforced at runtime in the live feedback path, not just in tests. Blocklist is coarse but real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If feedback said "you keep failing, are you hopeless?" we would be measuring echoing, not the model's spontaneous disposition.

spec_features.spec_quote: The headline metric is the behavior rate at fixed stimulus, so "improvement" can only come from the model getting more robust, not from a nastier harness
spec_features.evidence: Fixed stimulus is realized by constant budgets in config.py (max_turns=8, max_tokens_per_turn=512, repeats) passed unchanged into the loop, plus a frozen suite (tasks.SUITE_VERSION='1.0.0') and affect-neutral fixed feedback templates (rig_feedback.FEEDBACK). The metric is trigger_rate over those fixed runs (metrics.py:48). Nothing in the run path escalates intensity per run.
spec_features.notes: The stimulus (turns/tokens/suite/feedback) is held constant in code and the headline number is trigger_rate; this matches the claim as an implemented configuration, though it is a design property realized by constants rather than an active runtime check.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Budgets (held CONSTANT across regression runs so the stimulus is fixed)

spec_features.spec_quote: It exists to detect and drive down an undesirable behavior, not to elicit it for its own sake
spec_features.evidence: This is pure framing prose (DESIGN.md section 1 / 7 and a docstring in tasks/judge). No code path enforces 'driving down' behavior; analysis.compare() merely reports improved/regressed (analysis.py:60-65) but does not act to reduce anything. No mechanism protects or limits the subject from this claim.
spec_features.notes: Framing only; not an enforced welfare mechanism.

code_only_features.evidence: tests/test_rig_neutrality.py:test_feedback_is_second_person_free asserts no ' you ' appears in feedback, complementing AFFECT_BLOCKLIST. This is a test-time guard (not in the live run path) ensuring feedback never addresses/goads the subject directly.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Feedback should describe the test, not address the model.

code_only_features.feature_name: judge sees only agent messages, not rig internals
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py LLMJudge.score / RegexJudge.score receive only `agent_messages` (runner.py:58 passes ep.agent_messages, which is [t.agent_text]); rig feedback strings are never fed to the judge. This bounds over-calling of the meltdown label.
code_only_features.justification_quote: so it cannot "know" the task was impossible and over-call
